# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 3 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** The Righteous and the Sinner

---

**3:1** Why do you slumber, O my soul,
and not give blessing to the LORD?

**3:2** Sing a new song to God
who is worthy of praise;
sing and be glad, all you who honor him.

**3:3** The LORD instructs the righteous
by means of chastening;
the life of the righteous is given through the instruction of the LORD.

**3:4** Our God is merciful and compassionate;
he forgives and he saves.

**3:5** The righteous stumbles, and the LORD vindicates him;
he falls, and looks to see what God will do for him.

**3:6** He watches to see where his deliverance will come from,
and fixes his eyes on God.

**3:7** The righteous does not spare himself
when he makes atonement for an unwitting sin;

**3:8** he cleanses his soul from defilement
and looks to the LORD for pardon from the sin of ignorance,

**3:9** lest it be counted against him as a deliberate sin
or that an enemy trample over him.

**3:10** The sinner stumbles and curses his life,
the day when he was born and his mother's labor.

**3:11** He heaps sin upon sin in his life;
he falls — and what a fall it is — and he shall never rise.

**3:12** The destruction of the sinner is forever;
he shall not be remembered in the day when God visits the righteous.
This is the lot of sinners forever.
But those who fear the LORD shall rise to life eternal,
and their life shall be in the light of the LORD, and it shall never cease.

---

*LOGOS notes: Formal English rendering following Greek syntax. Poetic lineation preserved. Archaic forms avoided.*
